The Platform
The Foundry.
A digital-first manufacturing system, built to industrialize extreme-temperature materials at scale.
The end-to-end advanced-materials platform that the next generation of aerospace, defense, energy, and industrial systems needs now.
Foundry 1, the first facility, is in development, with more facilities to follow as the platform scales.
The Bottleneck
Advanced systems are being designed around materials the industrial base cannot yet produce economically.
The most ambitious next-generation aerospace and defense systems are not limited by performance. They are limited by the economics of producing advanced ceramic composites at scale.
Radian is building the scalable manufacturing platform to change that.
Demystifying the Technology
Ceramic Matrix Composites.
CMCs combine ceramic heat resistance with composite strength and low weight, reshaping high-performance systems. The advanced composites market is converging around one critical material.
70%
Lighter than advanced superalloys.
300°C
Higher maximum operating temperature.
You already rely on ceramic composites. The same family of materials turns up wherever heat, speed, and reuse meet:
Jet engine hot sections
Turbine shrouds and blades that run hotter and lighter, for more thrust and better fuel burn.
High-performance car brakes
Carbon-ceramic discs that take repeated extreme heat without fading and last far longer than steel.
Rocket nozzles and re-entry shields
Surfaces that survive re-entry-grade temperatures and can fly again.
The ambition of modern engineering has outpaced the economics of manufacturing.
“Ceramic matrix composites are poised to be the next material revolution… Analogous to carbon fiber reinforced composites in the mid-80s, CMCs are poised for explosive growth.”
Dr. David E. Glass, Senior Technologist, Applied Materials for Space and Hypersonics, NASA Langley Research Center
Source: NASA conference presentation, 2024
The Solution
A digital-first manufacturing system, built to industrialize CMCs at scale.
An independent, automated, end to end CMC production line, open to every customer.
Purpose-built to improve yield, increase cadence, and structurally compress cost. Fabrication, thermal processing, finishing, quality control, and digital process control
one integrated platform. This is how scalable CMC production becomes a national capability.
Integrated Production Chain
Preform fabrication, densification, and inspection engineered as one coordinated system, not siloed steps.
AI and Robotic Automation from Day One
Robotics, controlled fiber placement, and programmable high-temperature processing designed to systematically reduce variability, scrap, and manual intervention.
Digital Production Layer
Process modeling, digital twins, and AI-enabled process control compress cycle time, stabilize throughput, and structurally lower cost to optimize yield.
Foundry 1
integrated production chain
AFP cell 1 Automated fiber placement lays composite onto tooling, replacing hand lay-up.
AFP cell 2 Second preform fabrication cell.
Pyrolysis furnace 1100°C, converts the polymer matrix to ceramic.
Graphitization furnaces 2400°C, densify the CMC to final form.
Digital twin Process modeling and yield optimization across the whole chain.

Every major piece of the Foundry's technology already exists. Radian is integrating it.
Inside the Foundry
The equipment, the process, the physics.
Automated fiber placement cells feed a multi-furnace, high-temperature processing chain that turns composite preforms into finished ceramic-composite parts.

Dur-E-Therm TPS
Radian's proprietary thermal protection system.
Hot-fired at NASA Glenn to ~1,480°C through repeated ascent and re-entry profiles, including two 120-minute hypersonic test runs. Patent pending.
Reusable, not ablative
Designed to survive repeated re-entry without burning away, unlike single-use ablative heat shields.
Beyond shuttle-era
Longer life, a wider operating envelope, and easier operability than legacy thermal protection.
Dual-use by design
One architecture serves re-entry heat shielding, cryogenic tank insulation, and terrestrial high-heat industry.
More on Dur-E-Therm
Testing performed at NASA facilities under Space Act Agreement. Does not imply NASA endorses Radian or its products. Tests were ground simulations of flight profiles.
Cost Economics

The Foundry is designed to succeed where CMC industrialization has stalled. It targets a ~50% reduction in manufacturing cost by improving three structural drivers of CMC economics.

How is HyvivaGrid different from a battery?
Is storing hydrogen at my home or business safe?
Yes. HyvivaGrid doesn t use high-pressure tanks. The hydrogen is stored in metal hydride, which keeps it stable and unpressurized. There s no risk of thermal runaway fires that can affect batteries.
How long can I store hydrogen energy?
Hours, days, months, or across seasons. Stored hydrogen doesn t discharge over time, so you can save summer surplus for winter, when solar output is lowest.
Does HyvivaGrid make me independent from the grid?
It can. For most people it greatly reduces what they pay the utility and keeps the power on during outages.

Converting electricity to hydrogen and back uses some energy. We achieve about 60% round trip efficiency. But once stored, the hydrogen loses nothing for decades.

HyvivaGrid is currently available in the EU.
